findings.evidence: Lines 204–206 identify the carrier with `Submodule.span ℤ (Set.range b)`, so `Submodule.subset_span (Set.mem_range_self i)` proves the memberships; lines 175–179 already use exactly this canonical construction for `ofBasis.basisElem`.
findings.fix: Define an `ofGramMatrix.basisElem` (or construct the membership proofs internally) and state the theorem directly on those canonical elements, with only `b`, `G`, `hG`, `i`, and `j` as parameters.
findings.issue: `integralForm_ofGramMatrix_apply` requires `hi` and `hj`, although membership of every `b i` in the constructed carrier follows unconditionally from `carrier_ofGramMatrix`; these proof parameters unnecessarily weaken usability and make the statement depend on arbitrary subtype witnesses.

summary: The Gram-matrix evaluation theorem exposes redundant membership proofs instead of using the canonical embedded basis elements already provided by the API.
